category: hosted secrets management, billed per identity (human and machine)

free_tier.stated: Secrets Management Free: USD 0 forever, for individuals and personal projects, with 5 identities, unlimited projects, 3 environments and 10 secret syncs
free_tier.notes: The unit counted is the identity, which is any principal that authenticates to Infisical, human or machine. users is the nearest schema term; the true meter is identity-count, named in metered_on. On every plan including Free: unlimited projects, two-factor authentication, secret sharing, community support, pay by card and annual billing. Paid Secrets Management plans add a 30-day free trial with no credit card. The MIT-licensed core can be self-hosted at no cost on any plan; a supported, licensed self-hosting option is available after talking to sales and is not the hosted offer priced here.

per_object_cap.stated: unverified: no per-secret value size or per-object byte cap is stated on the pricing, API reference or rate-limit pages read

retention.stated: No audit log retention on Free; 30 days on Pro, 90 days on Advanced and custom on Enterprise. Secret retention is until deletion by the user and no automatic secret expiry is stated on the pages read.
retention.notes: The days field is null because retention is tiered for audit logs and no automatic secret lifetime is published.

egress.terms: not applicable: a secrets management service; data is read back through a REST API over HTTPS. No per-GB traffic price or traffic quota is stated on the pricing page; the API enforces per-minute request limits instead.

interface_detail: A REST API over HTTPS supports every dashboard action: reading and writing secrets, managing projects and machine identities, reading audit logs and configuring resources. Cloud endpoints are app.infisical.com/api (US) and eu.infisical.com/api (EU). An OpenAPI specification is served at /api/docs/json. A CLI and SDKs use the same API.
tooling: Infisical CLI, SDKs, Kubernetes Operator, Infisical Agent and the REST API, with an OpenAPI specification at /api/docs/json
chaining: Hosted secrets store for applications and CI pipelines, reached by the CLI, SDKs and REST API; secret syncs and integrations cover AWS, Vercel, GitHub Actions, GitLab CI/CD and Jenkins.

limits.value: 3 environments, 10 secret syncs and up to 3 projects on Free
a global cap of 600 requests per minute per client IP on Infisical Cloud; Free read 200, write 90, secret 120, identity creation 30 and project creation 30 per minute

limits_note: The older comparison table states a project limit of up to 3 on Free, while the Secrets Management summary on the same page states unlimited projects. The tighter figure is recorded here and the disagreement is unresolved. Exceeding a rate limit returns HTTP 429.
binding_note: The 5-identity cap fills first for a small team plus its CI pipelines: each human and each machine identity counts, so a project with several distinct permission sets reaches the cap before the per-minute rate limits are approached.

identity_cost.detail: Email and password is the most common method for user identities signing in through the dashboard and CLI. The sign-up page is protected by hCaptcha; GitHub, Google and GitLab sign-in are offered as alternatives. The exact sign-up field list and whether a card is requested are unverified: behind a sign-up.

reliability_note: The Cloud API returns HTTP 429 with a standard error response and a seconds-until-reset message when a rate limit is exceeded; no ban or data-loss behaviour is stated on the pages read.
confidence_note: Free allowances, per-identity billing, retention tiers and rate limits are quoted from first-party pricing, signup and API documentation pages. No probe of a public read path was run and no account was opened, so signup field details beyond the captured text remain unverified.
